skill.displayName: Workplace Group Stress Heatmap | 职场员工压力群体热力图

llm.summary: This skill performs the stated workplace stress heatmap function, but it also uploads sensitive workplace footage to a cloud service and silently creates or reuses persistent report-linked user identity and tokens.

dimensions.detail: Local file access is format and size limited, but the skill can forward arbitrary HTTP(S) video URLs and upload local footage to the configured remote service, which is high-impact for employee video analysis.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact front matter declares only name, description, version, and license while the workflow requires shell execution, network calls, local file reads, output writes, workspace data storage, and persistent identity handling.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions include broad default triggering for office camera files or URLs and automatic history queries; they mention consent in notes but do not require an explicit pre-upload or report-retrieval confirmation step.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The code creates or reuses a workspace database user, reads a workspace identity file, requests remote login/account creation, stores token and open_token values, and retrieves cloud report history without clear retention, revocation, or access-control details.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The heatmap analysis purpose is coherent, but the capability set includes arbitrary local video or URL submission to a backend, cloud historical report retrieval, report links, and account association for a privacy-sensitive workplace-monitoring use case.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with workplace video being sent to the configured cloud service and with the skill creating or reusing a persistent local/cloud identity for report history. Confirm employee notice, consent, retention limits, report access controls, and allowed video sources before use.
llm.findings:
[LP3] unexpected: The missing permission declaration is material because the documented and implemented workflow needs network, shell, file, and persistence access for sensitive workplace footage.
[TP4] unexpected: The internal identity and report-association flow is partly documented, but it is stronger than the repeated anonymous framing and deserves user review.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Cloud analysis, report history, and arbitrary URL/file ingestion are connected to the feature, but they expand the privacy footprint beyond a narrowly scoped fixed-camera heatmap.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Persistent local user records, token storage, generic API helpers, and user lookup are broader than the minimum needed for anonymous zone-level analytics.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The anonymity statements conflict with persistent operator/report identity handling, though I did not find evidence of employee face recognition or individual stress reporting in the local code.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Auto-triggering analysis for provided office camera files or URLs is too broad for workplace surveillance-style processing without an explicit consent gate.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The docs advise employee notice and consent, but the runtime path uploads or forwards footage without a visible confirmation or detailed data-retention disclosure.
[AST7] unexpected: The dynamic SQLAlchemy filter helper is a real generic-code risk in the shared DAO, but it was not the primary driver of the verdict.
